Two is-a steps (aorta, artery, blood vessel). Obvious.
An RNA primer is itself a polymer; 'overlaps' is the weakest relation. Four premises for nothing.
Excitatory (Na+/cation) channels only. GABA-A and glycine receptors are ligand-gated Cl- channels that hyperpolarise; class is overgeneral.
Same fact as the base PNS term, narrowed to vertebrates.
Same fact for a narrower context (Metazoa). Loose: the system raises oxygen in the body, not in the air.
Every cell has ribosomes; reached by a detour through mitoribosomes. Weak 'overlaps'. Term is nervous system, premise says nervous tissue.
tRNA has ribothymidine (m5U54) in the T-loop, so it does contain thymine. Book rule 'RNA has no thymine' is a simplification. Rated as if true: restates RNA premise.
Narrow-context restatement. Ribosomes are machinery, not an input; 'requires' is the real sense.
Weaker than the premise chain: basal ganglia are part of the CNS, not just overlapping it.
Same shape as the tRNA-uracil worked example.
2'-OH of ribose (also 3'-OH, phosphate OH). Obvious.
True anatomically (aorta lies by the vena cava) but the route is wrong: premise is 'some animals' counter-current heat exchange in limbs, not the aorta.
Narrow-context restatement of a base chromosome fact.
Every nucleated cell overlaps a chromosome. Neuron adds nothing.
Flatworm ganglion vs UBERON gray matter (a vertebrate CNS term). Class-level overlap via 'cell body'; invertebrates use cell-body rind and neuropil.
Axonemal and spindle microtubules are different instances; class-level overlap via 'microtubule' is false as 'shares a part'. Startling if true. Prokaryotic flagella have no microtubules either.
Trivial and absurd: everything has carbon. Seven-step chain through plasma membrane sugars.
Narrow-context restatement; DNA is a polymer. Premise 'chromosome within the nucleus' does not hold for prokaryotes.
Class-level supply claim: arteries carry oxygen, lungs raise it (pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood). Sign is right if read as oxygen delivery; EPO is set by kidney oxygen sensing.
Only true because the book (and GO) put the plasma membrane inside the endomembrane system. Weaker than 'passive transport happens in plasma membrane'. Misleading to a student.
Trivial, weak 'overlaps'. True of incorporated ribonucleotides; free ATP/GTP are not in a polymer.
Every cell has a plasma membrane. Generic.
Weaker than the premise chain: amygdala is part of the brain.
Telomerase has an RNA component; RNA is a nucleic acid. Route via ribose is pointless.
True only by the book/GO convention that the plasma membrane is endomembrane (many texts exclude it). A student would think of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Generic subject (organ system); cells make ATP.
Trivial: mitochondrial DNA is a polymer.
True (degranulation, cytokines), but the route is unsound: the premise secretors are antibody-secreting plasma cells, not neutrophils.
Same as the aldosterone premise, narrowed to blood. Standard teaching (low Na+ raises aldosterone); K+ and angiotensin II matter more.
Vessels deliver oxygen; oxygen drives the ETC. Same type as capillaries promote aerobic respiration. Generic 'blood vessel' is loose (veins carry little oxygen).
Weak 'overlaps' for generic muscle organ. Cardiac and smooth muscle have no skeletal muscle tissue; smooth muscle has no sarcomeres.
Narrow-context restatement. 'Limbic system' is a mammalian concept; homologues in other vertebrates are debated. Book is human.
A venule is itself a blood vessel; trivial.
Wrong term: label says deficient, term is telomerase activity (in mouse). Read as the term it is a restated premise (true); read as labelled it would be false and startling.
Context error: oxygen in a leaf cannot lower a mammalian kidney hormone (plants have no EPO). Startling if true. Base fact is about blood oxygen.
Unreadable relation 'can carry out arise from'. Probably 'takes part in cell division'; cytoskeletal parts do (spindle, contractile ring).
Two is-a steps. In ChEBI, nutrient is a role, not a class of ions.
Aorta is itself a blood vessel; 'connected to' is trivial.
Generic subject; enterocytes endocytose. Route through 'cells can phagocytose'.

Every nucleated cell has ribosomal subunits; detour via mitoribosomes. GO term is the cytosolic small subunit, mitochondria have their own (GO mitochondrial small ribosomal subunit). Term is nervous system, premise says nervous tissue.
Narrow-context restatement of a premise. Subject label 'These reactions' is an unresolved pointer; unreadable on its own.
Generic subject. Premise is about accessory organs of the digestive system; the heart does not promote digestion. Wrong term: should be digestive accessory organ.
Weaker than 'alveoli are next to capillaries'.
Weaker than the premise chain: brainstem is part of the CNS.
Obsolete CL term (obsolete animal cell). Generic, weak 'overlaps'; plasma membrane counts as endomembrane only by the book's convention.
Two part-of steps. 'Forearm' here means the forearm bones; UBERON zeugopod is a body segment, a slight stretch for a skeleton part.
Same shape as the tRNA-uracil worked example.
Already a sentence in the book (premise 1 says they attach to the plasma membrane).
Two premises joined; obvious.
Weaker than 'happens in ATP synthase'. 'Integral membrane protein' mapped to 'membrane protein complex'; ATP synthase is a complex, so the name is close but not the same.
Two part-of steps.
Arteries are blood vessels; trivial and weaker than the premise.
The definition of rough ER: ribosome-studded, so it makes proteins. Obvious.
Glucose promotes its own import through insulin: a feedback loop a teacher might use. Insulin-dependent import is in muscle and fat, not all cells.
Narrow-context restatement. Weak: the point is that meiosis outputs haploid nuclei.
Dietary fat aids absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, not nutrients in general (fat slows gastric emptying and glucose uptake). Term 'intestinal absorption' is wider than the premise.
Narrow-context restatement.
Two premises joined. Smooth muscle has myofilaments too, though not in sarcomeres.
Weaker than 'gene expression gives RNA as output'; leaves out protein.
Narrow-context restatement. ATP synthase is a multi-subunit complex (F1 peripheral, Fo integral), so 'membrane protein complex' is the better name than 'integral membrane protein'.
Catabolism does not contain anabolism: 'has part anabolism' belongs to metabolism as a whole and was pushed down to one half of it. 'Broken down' is also an unresolved pointer. Startling if true.
Restates a premise for a narrower context. Obsolete CL term.
Weaker than the premise, which lists the thalamus as a brain part; reached by a detour via the limbic system.
Sarcolemma is a plasma membrane; plasma membranes transport. Obvious.
Brain has basal ganglia; basal ganglia control movement. Obvious.
Silly context (BLN:hot_dry_day); plants have DNA on any day. Trivial; detour via mitochondrial DNA.
Equivocation on 'bacteria': immune cells fight invaders, the colon flora are tolerated and help digestion. Startling if true.
Already a book sentence (neuron cell body contains Golgi); every cell has Golgi.
Chromatin is the eukaryotic DNA-histone complex in the nucleus; the book's own definition says so. Bacteria have a nucleoid, though archaea do have histone chromatin. Startling if true.
Depolarisation opens Na+ channels so Na+ enters: the positive feedback of the action potential. 'Amount of sodium' is intracellular only.

Anaphor 'These atoms' joins two pathways: the glucose sentence is respiration, the NADPH one is the Calvin cycle. NADPH hydrogen is passed to the sugar (transfer, not a shared part). Both hold hydrogen, so 'overlaps' is empty.
Loop with a spurious sign: insulin lowers glucose, which lowers insulin secretion, so net insulin lowers insulin. The path via glucagon gives 'raises'. Odd context on the object (beta cell).
Plainly false: eukaryotic chromosomes sit in the nucleus. The premise is about prokaryotes; a negative on the generic term was pushed down into Eukaryota.
Membranes regulate: they block some things and let others pass. One-sided, and it contradicts R065.
Same equivocation as R068 (invaders versus gut flora), narrower subject.
Narrow-context restatement. The premise 'chromosome within the nucleus' is wrong for prokaryotes but the conclusion holds.
Oxidative phosphorylation makes ATP; ATP powers contraction. Same type as ATP synthase promotes muscle contraction. Fast bursts run on glycolysis and creatine phosphate.
Restates a book sentence. Book and GO include the plasma membrane in the endomembrane system; many texts do not.
Generic subject; every gland has cells with plasma membranes.
True of metabolic poisons that cut the ATP supply (cyanide, ouabain acts directly). Generic 'poison' is too wide: tetrodotoxin blocks Na+ channels, other poisons act elsewhere.
Trivial and absurd route: ribosome polypeptides inside mitochondria. Amino acids are in every cell.
Two premises joined; obvious.
Narrow-context restatement. Pumps in the plasma membrane do active transport; the premise only says 'actively bringing in'.
Membrane integrity prevents lysis. But the plasma membrane also executes some deaths (gasdermin pores, MLKL, complement) and carries death receptors.
Trivial. Obsolete CL term.
Three part-of steps, each standard. Hippocampal formation is archicortex of the temporal lobe.
Generic subject (cell); phospholipid tails.
Same type as R031 and the capillaries-aerobic respiration example: vessels deliver oxygen, oxygen drives oxidative phosphorylation. 'A process' is an unresolved pointer.
Equivocation on 'sugars': membrane glycans versus dietary sugar. Meat is muscle, but muscle tissue as a class is not food. Startling if true.
Narrow-context restatement of the book definition of chromosome.
Weak: a part inherits what the whole does. True by the plasma-membrane-is-endomembrane convention.
Two part-of steps; anyone sees it at once.
Trivial: lysosomes are in cells, cells transport.
Generic and trivial. Obsolete CL term.
Weaker than the premise (temporal lobe is part of the cortex; the book is loose, lobes include white matter).
Chemiosmosis in bacteria is real (plasma membrane, not the mitochondrial membrane in the premise). 'These reactions' is an unresolved pointer. Fermenting prokaryotes lack an ETC.
Many ion channels are in the plasma membrane, but class-wide it fails: mitochondrial and bacterial channels are not endomembrane. Also rests on the plasma-membrane convention.
Human skeleton only (fish have no sacrum). Three part-of steps.
Narrow-context restatement of a book sentence.
